To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the overall size of an excluded volume chain confined between two plates is nonmonotonic as a function of the plate separation, with a minimum at intermediate separations, and that (2) the size of the chain in a plane parallel with the plates is monotonic, increasing with increasing plate separation, in contrast to recent experimental results.

the size of a polymer confined between two parallel planes depends on the plate separation and the polymer size in the confined direction, but not on the polymer size in an unconfined direction, and that the size in the confined directions is non-monotonic as a function of the plate separation.
the overall size of a polymer confined between two plates is a monotonic function of the plate separation, while the size of the confined polymer is nonmonotonic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the size and shape of excluded-volume polymers confined between plates.
the behavior of a single polymer chain in a narrow channel between two parallel plates.
the problem of a polymer chain confined between parallel plates of a given separation and with the question whether the chain is stretched or compressed in the confined direction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the overall size of a chain is predicted to be nonmonotonic as a function of the plate separation and that the size in the confined plane is predicted to be a monotonic function, but the experimental data are not in agreement with these predictions.

the overall size and shape of the polymer chain are in good agreement with the scaling predictions and the mean-field theory, whereas the behavior of the chain size in the plane of confinement is in disagreement with the scaling theory but in good agreement with our mean-field theory.
the size of the chain, as measured by the end-to-end distance, is monotonic as a function of the confinement strength (the plate separation) for all plate separations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nonmonotonous behavior of the polymer size as a function of confinement strength is not due to a nonmonotonous change in the polymer size in the plane parallel to the confining plates.
the size of the chain in the plane parallel to the confining plates is predicted to be larger than the size of the same chain in the absence of confinement.
the nonmonotonous behavior of the polymer size is a consequence of the excluded volume interaction, but it is the confinement that makes it possible to observe the effect experimentally.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the crossover between the two regimes can be captured by a simple scaling argument.

, in order to understand the behavior of a long polymer chain under confinement, it is crucial to take into account the anisotropic shape of the chain, which is determined by the competition between the excluded volume and the confinement.
, while the mean-field theory captures the essential physics of polymer confinement, it is not sufficient to explain all the experimental observations.
